subject: Bering Strait dam
title: What If We Dammed the Bering Strait? A Soviet Plan to Melt the Arctic

scenes.text: What if we dammed the sea between Russia and Alaska to melt the Arctic? The Soviets drew plans.
In the 1950s, Petr Borisov proposed a wall across the 55-mile Bering Strait: concrete sections 820 feet long, sunk 200 feet deep.
Pumps run by a 2,000-megawatt nuclear plant would push cold Arctic water south into the Pacific.
Warm, salty Atlantic water would flow in behind it. Dark open water soaks up sunlight, so the ice would melt and never return.
His price: about 70 billion rubles. His promise: hundreds of millions of hectares of Siberia thawed. In 1960, Senator Kennedy called it worth exploring.
Soviet climatologists warned Europe could dry out and African winters cool by five degrees. It was never built. The Arctic is melting anyway.

description:
What if we dammed the Bering Strait? In the 1950s Soviet engineer Petr Borisov proposed exactly that: a dam across the 55-mile strait, with nuclear-powered pumps pushing cold Arctic water into the Pacific so warm Atlantic water could flow in and melt the ice for good.
He estimated the cost at about 70 billion rubles and promised to thaw hundreds of millions of hectares of Siberia. Senator John F. Kennedy called the idea worth exploring in 1960. Soviet climatologists warned it could dry out Europe and cool African winters by about 5 degrees, and it was never built.
What should we run through next?
thumbnail_text: WHAT IF WE MELTED THE ARCTIC?
first_comment: Borisov wanted the US, Canada and Japan to help pay, and the dam would have doubled as a road and railway between the continents. Which giant plan should we run through next?
